title: Create and read one Client offline through Supabase, PowerSync, the target app, and target MCP

requirements.invariant: An authorized create allocates one stable Account-scoped Client identity and required display name; equal names remain distinct when Client IDs differ, and name text never becomes identity or authorization.

The target app accepts Client creation with no network, stores the operation and optimistic row atomically in an encrypted per-Principal/Account database, renders it immediately as non-authoritative, and preserves it across close/reopen until synchronized or explicitly discarded by the separate logout policy.

The trusted Postgres handler re-derives the authenticated Principal and active Client-management membership, permits no direct Client/result writes, exposes only Account-authorized reads, and does not reveal another Account's Client or operation existence.

One canonical client-create-v1 envelope binds Operation, Account, actor, Client, display name, capture time and empty preconditions; exact replay returns one immutable terminal result, changed replay fails, and durable validation rejection drains rather than poisons the upload queue.

The target app and gated target MCP tool use the same Client command bytes, fingerprint, RPC and terminal-result validation; MCP scope comes from authenticated context and neither path uses a service-role credential.

All provider work remains spike_-prefixed, synthetic and isolated from hosted and production systems; it changes no Firebase implementation, grants no migration/cutover authority, and leaves A-003/A-004 proposed until the full spike exit gate passes.

items: Reuse ClientCreationDraft, CreateClientCommand, ClientCreationOperating and ClientCoreDetailsQuerying without provider types crossing into LedgerTargetCore.
Use one canonical sorted JSON envelope with milliseconds-since-epoch dates and one SHA-256 fingerprint shared by Swift, MCP and the trusted handler.
spike_principals maps auth.users to stable Principals; spike_accounts and spike_account_memberships own active Client-management capability.
spike_clients stores stable identity, Account FK, name, lifecycle, revision and server-authored audit evidence with lookup/FK indexes.
spike_operation_results stores one immutable applied/rejected result per OperationID with exact fingerprint, subject, times and terminal code.
ledger_private.spike_create_client authenticates and authorizes before taking a transaction-scoped OperationID advisory lock.
Exact replay returns the stored result; payload rebinding raises conflict; permanent payload validation persists a rejected result; accepted input inserts Client and result atomically.
public.spike_create_client is the sole security-invoker Data API entry and delegates to the private trusted handler.
anon and authenticated receive no table write privilege; authenticated receives only SELECT on the five spike tables and EXECUTE on the public RPC plus required private helpers.
public, anon and authenticated receive no broad ledger_private schema or function privilege beyond explicit helper/RPC execution.
RLS is enabled on every public spike relation; Principal is self-only, membership is self/current-active, and Account/Client/result visibility requires active Account membership.
Client mutation requires the trusted handler's active can_manage_clients check; restricted and cross-account identities fail without direct-write fallback.
Edition-3 streams derive the Principal from auth.user_id(), synchronize active memberships and Accounts, and scope Clients/results through those memberships.
A live PowerSync Sync Stream validation and readback remains required before A-004 can advance.
PowerSync opens only through an absolute .sqlite path and 256-bit SQLCipher key loaded from a this-device-only per-Principal/Account Keychain namespace.
Offline acceptance writes local operation evidence, optimistic Client and insert-only command in one transaction and survives close/reopen with encrypted bytes.
Pending optimism forces partial readiness even after an earlier sync; terminal applied/rejected upload updates local operation state only after a matching server result.

storageMedia.notApplicable: Client creation owns no attachment. S6 media durability remains a separate full-spike obligation and A-003/A-004 cannot advance from this Client slice alone.

items: The isolated target staging shell opens the encrypted local runtime and can create/watch a synthetic Account-scoped Client while permanently showing LOCAL SPIKE / NO HOSTED SERVICES.

The gated target create_client MCP tool derives Account/Principal from request context, validates input and exact terminal result, and calls the same Supabase RPC with user token plus publishable key.
Swift and TypeScript pin an identical canonical envelope and SHA-256 fingerprint fixture.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase snapshot is read or imported. Final Client synthesis/correlation remains a separate migration slice and this spike is not migration authorization.

items: Local tests expose only bounded pass/fail and stable error codes; token, key, Client name and command payload logging is prohibited.
A later connected rehearsal must record operation correlation, sync latency, retry count and terminal state without private payloads.
The slice exists only in the separate target worktree/app and spike_-prefixed local schema; Firebase remains unchanged and authoritative.
The client_management capability and create_client contract remain gated; no hosted resource, deployment, release, migration or production switch is performed.
Rollback during the spike is disposal of the isolated local target database/configuration; source data is never touched.

verification.expected: A clean local reset passes all 19 schema, handler, replay, immutability, authorization, timestamp-binding/overflow-rejection and tenant-isolation assertions.
Offline create is atomic, encrypted, immediately queryable as partial, durable across close/reopen, idempotent, and produces exactly one validated two-entry upload transaction.
Changed replay and malformed transaction/result fail closed, while a durable server rejection drains once, records rejected locally, and cannot poison later queued operations.
Swift and MCP share exact command bytes/hash; both adapters send scoped user credentials and reject mismatched result identity before completion.
The local Data API applies and replays once for an owner, hides the row from another Account, rejects a restricted member, and denies direct table insertion.
Immutable CI passes local Supabase DB/API tests, target/MCP tests, environment checks and both staging builds with a clean worktree.

verification.owner: Future isolated hosted PowerSync vertical-spike rehearsal
verification.expected: A real authenticated device uploads offline Client creation, receives authoritative Client/result rows, preserves tenant isolation, survives fault repetition, and records cost/latency evidence without production access.
Exact OperationID replay returns the immutable terminal result with one Client/result row, while changed payload reuse cannot rebind the OperationID.
An authenticated active Client manager can call the RPC and read the resulting Client and terminal operation result in the same Account.
Provider-free Client commands and read snapshots retain exact Account/actor/Client/name/time/revision/readiness contracts and reject malformed or rebound evidence.

verification.owner: Supabase Postgres security, indexing and locking best-practices review
verification.expected: Schema review confirms indexed foreign keys and RLS predicates, least-privilege grants, private security-definer helpers, explicit auth checks and transaction-scoped locking with no unresolved high-risk finding.

verification.owner: Future isolated authenticated target app and MCP rehearsal
verification.expected: The app accepts offline, reconnects through real PowerSync, reaches the trusted Supabase handler, receives authoritative readback, and the MCP path produces the same result without production access.

notes: The local implementation path is working and test-backed, but this dossier deliberately remains in_progress. A-003/A-004 remain proposed until the full isolated vertical spike, including real Sync Streams/Auth/device/media/evolution/performance/failure phases, passes. No isolated hosted Supabase/PowerSync environment or target authentication strategy has been authorized or provisioned. This grants no hosted, migration, cutover or production authority.
